name: פירוק טרינום ריבועי עם מקדם מוביל – גורמים בסימנים מנוגדים (באנגלית)
generalfeedback:
Factorising a quadratic with an \(x^2\) coefficient which is not equal to 1 is slightly more complex. As can be seen by multiplying out a general, factorised quadratic:
\[ (cx+a)(dx+b) = cdx^2+(da+cb)x+ab. \]
\(a\) and \(b\) are still factors of the constant term, and \(c\) and \(d\) are factors of the \(x^2\) coefficient so there are still only a finite number of (integer) cases that are possible. With practice it should still be simple enough to find \(a\), \(b\), \(c\) and \(d\).

In this example:

\[ {{CT:0}}. \]
Equating with the general quadratic above gives:
\[{cd = {{CT:1}}}.\]
\[{da+cb = {{CT:2}}}.\]
\[{ab = {{CT:3}}}.\]

The correct values are: \(a = {{CT:4}}\), and \(b = {{CT:5}}\), \(c = {{CT:6}}\) and, \(d = {{CT:7}}\). By substituting these back into the general quadratic, and factorising constants out, we obtain the factored form: \[{{CT:8}}.\]
